# horsie_routine (Resource)

An agent preset plus a fixed prompt and a trigger.

Running one creates an unattended session that works from the prompt alone. Those sessions are listed under the routine, never in the session list.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "horsie_routine" "nightly" {
  name   = "nightly-review"
  agent  = horsie_agent.reviewer.name
  prompt = "Review anything that landed today and summarise what needs attention."

  # Required: horsie has no default for where a run happens.
  environment {
    type   = "runtime"
    vendor = "local"
  }

  schedule {
    type     = "daily"
    timezone = "UTC"
    hour     = 3
    minute   = 30
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `agent` (String) Name of the `horsie_agent` preset every run is configured from. Reference the resource's `name` so Terraform orders the two correctly.
- `name` (String) Slug used in API paths. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `prompt` (String) The message queued as each run's first user message.

### Optional

- `description` (String) What this routine is for. Defaults to empty.
- `enabled` (Boolean) False pauses the timer. Triggering by hand still works, which is why this pauses rather than disables.
- `environment` (Block, Optional) Where each run happens and what it runs against. **Required** — horsie has no default, because an optional environment would be a second, invisible way to answer the question, settled by a server default nobody asked for. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--environment))
- `schedule` (Block, Optional) When the routine fires by itself. Omit for a manual routine. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--schedule))

### Read-Only

- `next_run_at_ms` (Number) When the timer fires next, unix epoch millis. Absent when nothing is scheduled — a manual routine, a paused one, or a spent `once`.

<a id="nestedblock--environment"></a>
### Nested Schema for `environment`

Required:

- `type` (String) `runtime` for an ad-hoc environment, or `named` for a `horsie_environment` by name.

Optional:

- `name` (String) `named`: the `horsie_environment` to use. It is resolved and snapshotted when a run is created, so editing or deleting it never re-points a run that exists.
- `repos` (Block List) `runtime`: repositories to check out. A vendor that cannot provision a workspace rejects a non-empty list at create. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--environment--repos))
- `vendor` (String) `runtime`: the runtime vendor. `local` is spelled here like any other vendor — there is no separate variant for it.

<a id="nestedblock--environment--repos"></a>
### Nested Schema for `environment.repos`

Required:

- `url` (String) HTTPS clone URL.

Optional:

- `dir` (String) Directory under the workspace.
- `git_ref` (String) Branch, tag or commit.



<a id="nestedblock--schedule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `schedule`

Required:

- `type` (String) One of `manual`, `every`, `once`, `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, `yearly`. Each type reads only the attributes it needs; setting one it does not use is an error rather than being silently ignored.

Optional:

- `at_ms` (Number) `once`: unix epoch millis. An instant already in the past never fires; move it forward to re-arm.
- `day_of_month` (Number) `monthly`/`yearly`: day of month. Months without that day are skipped entirely.
- `hour` (Number) Hour of day, 0–23.
- `interval_seconds` (Number) `every`: seconds between runs, minimum 60. The next run is scheduled from when the previous one fired, so a server that was down resumes with one run rather than a backlog.
- `minute` (Number) Minute of hour, 0–59.
- `month` (Number) `yearly`: month, 1–12.
- `timezone` (String) `daily`/`weekly`/`monthly`/`yearly`: IANA timezone, e.g. `Europe/London`.
- `weekdays` (List of String) `weekly`: at least one of `Mon`…`Sun`. Duplicates are rejected.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Resources are addressed by their name/alias, which is the id of record.
terraform import horsie_routine.example nightly-review
```
